product: BodyJ4You Organic Castor Oil Roll-On 1.7 oz, rose quartz roller
hand_block: The only person is one woman, seen as hands and forearms only: warm light-medium brown skin, smooth even skin, slim fingers. Her nails are SHORT natural-length rounded nails, trimmed level with the fingertips, painted sheer glossy nude. Every hand enters from a frame edge with the whole wrist visible. A hand that touches the bottle GRIPS it with curled fingers around the glass. No face, no neck, no other people.
scene_block: Setting: a bright, clean home with soft natural daylight from a window on the left, white and light neutral surfaces, airy and fresh. Shot on a phone, natural light, realistic unretouched skin texture, neutral white balance, bright exposure, no cinematic grading, no warm golden or yellow cast, no dark shadows. No on-screen text or captions. No other branded products. No reflection of a person.
prod_block: The product is exactly the BodyJ4You castor oil roll-on in the product reference images: a short, wide cylindrical dark amber-brown glass bottle with a threaded glass neck, a white plastic collar holding a smooth, clearly soft-pink rose quartz ball (pink, not white or peach) on top (no cap anywhere); a wrap-around white label with plum-purple bands at top and bottom, the small 'Body4You' logo, '100% Premium Quality', a large plum serif 'CASTOR OIL', a round green-and-white USDA ORGANIC seal, 'CERTIFIED ORGANIC' and '1.7 FL OZ / 50 ML'. The bottle keeps this exact shape, colours and label layout in every frame: no morphing, no extra text, no label drift, no cap.
video_suffix: Fingers move naturally and stay anatomically correct (five fingers per hand). The bottle and its label stay exactly the same shape and layout. No sound. No on-screen text.

shots.vo: If you are wondering whether castor oil is only for babies, here you go.
shots.still: Close-up on a bright white marble bathroom vanity top: the BodyJ4You castor roll-on stands upright in the centre, label facing the lens, sharp and readable; her right hand enters from the bottom right edge and her fingers curl around the amber glass body below the label edge, about to lift it. A blurred white towel and a small glass tray behind.
shots.video: Shot 1: the hand lifts the roll-on off the vanity and brings it a little toward the lens, tilting it so the pink rose quartz ball faces the camera, then holds it steady. Slow, natural, handheld phone feel.

shots.vo: I used castor oil to get my daughter's cradle cap out. But did you know people use it everywhere?
shots.note: Grace's own viral clip, cropped tight on the baby's head + her comb hand, no product, no other brand, no TikTok logo

shots.vo: The problem is it's thick and drips all over your fingers.
shots.still: Close-up over a white bathroom sink: her left hand enters from the left edge holding a plain CLEAR unlabeled glass bottle tilted down, a thick slow ribbon of pale golden oil pours onto the two fingertips of her right hand, which enters from the bottom edge; oil already runs down between her fingers and a drop hangs from the knuckle. shots.vo: This one rolls on with a rose quartz roller.
